Business-Rule coverage of the AI team's 5-10 scenario delivery

Denominator is each network's own Test BR (supporting-rule) catalog, built by the AI team from the 5-10 run and read directly from each package's requirements_scenarios/scenario_supporting_rules.csv. Executive summary

Just over a third of grounding Test BRs are confirmed across all 5 networks

The 5-10 AI run built five network packages: American Express Credit (36 scenarios, 601 test cases), MasterCard Credit (36 scenarios, 630 test cases), MasterCard Fleet (24 scenarios, 339 test cases), Interlink Debit (24 scenarios, 323 test cases) and Maestro Direct Debit (24 scenarios, 323 test cases). Each package carries its own Test BR catalog — the ATL105 spec rules the AI grounded its scenarios in (scenario_supporting_rules.csv). Of the combined 2,755 Test BRs across all five packages, 1,036 (37.60%) carry no “requires review” flag and are treated here as confirmed-covered; the remaining 1,719 (62.40%) require SME or QA review before they can be counted as covered.

What this number is, and is not

This is package-scoped candidate coverage: the denominator is each package's own AI-built supporting-rule catalog, not the separate 1,343-row independent Test Solution BR catalog (which uses a different segment-anchored ID scheme and is not joined here). It also is not semantic approval, SME sign-off, or execution/pass status — all 5 packages are explicitly marked mapping_status = candidate in their build metadata.

This exact population is under open defect review

The independent 10 Nov delivery-gate run (2026-11-10-5-10-delivery-gates-v1/validation.json) returns gate = FAIL, execution readiness = BLOCKED, semantic certification = NOT_CERTIFIED for all 5 packages. Separately, the Round 3 revalidation of this same delivery (Consolidated_Revalidation_AllProducts_2026-11-06_Round3.md) found no regressions anywhere: every defect confirmed fixed in Round 2 held up, but of ~19 previously open items only one (MC Fleet's CD-19) turned out to already be fine — the rest remain open, plus 2 newly surfaced items. Treat the coverage figures on this page as a structural, rule-grounding snapshot of the 5-10 delivery, not a certified or execution-ready result.

Methodology and limitations

Read this as package-scoped rule-grounding confidence, not semantic coverage

  • Denominator (“Test BR”): the distinct rule_id rows in each network's own requirements_scenarios/scenario_supporting_rules.csv — the ATL105 spec rules the AI's scenario generator cited as grounding for that network's scenarios. American Express Credit = 510, MasterCard Credit = 590, MasterCard Fleet = 814, Interlink Debit = 423, Maestro Direct Debit = 418.
  • Numerator (“covered”): rules in that same file with no requires_review flag set. All rules in the file already have scenario_count ≥ 1 by construction (unreferenced rules are not listed), so this is a confidence/review measure layered on top of baseline linkage, not a reach/non-reach measure.
  • Extends the 31 Oct precedent: this page reuses, without modification, the exact denominator/numerator definition from reports/2026-10-31-ai-team-delivery-defects/MASTERCARD-BR-COVERAGE-REPORT-31-OCT-2026.html (which covered Mastercard Credit and Fleet only) and extends it to American Express Credit, Interlink Debit and Maestro Direct Debit for the first time, using the newer 5-10 delivery for all 5 networks.
  • Why this is not joined to the independent 1,343-row Test Solution BR catalog: that catalog uses segment-anchored IDs (for example BR-RULE-SEG104-R-002), while this delivery's rule catalog uses page-anchored IDs (for example BR-104-2). The two ID schemes do not share a key, and no crosswalk file linking them was found for the 5-10 output. Building one would require the same token/segment-matching engine used in the 2026-10-14 AI-to-Test-BR crosswalk report, which is intentionally out of scope for this page.
  • Build state: all 5 packages carry mapping_status = "candidate" and state = "CANDIDATE" in their build metadata. No SME or Test Solution owner has adjudicated MATCH/PARTIAL/NOT_MATCH against this rule set.
  • Scope exclusions: 524 scenario combinations across the 5 networks were deliberately excluded as not applicable and are outside every count on this page.
  • This page does not assert test execution, pass/fail status, or production behavior. It also does not supersede or close any open item in the 10 Nov delivery-gate run or the Round 3 revalidation report.

Decision requested

Treat 37.60% as package-scoped, candidate rule-grounding confidence for the 5-10 delivery across all 5 network types — not certified BR coverage against the independent 1,343-row Test Solution baseline, and not a statement that execution is unblocked (the 10 Nov gate reports BLOCKED for every network).

Nominate SME reviewers for the 1,719 combined Test BRs still flagged requires_review (308 AMEX Credit, 354 MC Credit, 537 MC Fleet, 262 Interlink Debit, 258 Maestro Debit), prioritizing the 1,083 rules scoring below 0.6 extraction confidence. In parallel, re-raise the two recurring structural gaps the Round 3 revalidation found unfixed across multiple networks — the Table 030/056/003 blank-length family (AMEX/MC Credit/MC Fleet) and the <AWAITING:...> placeholder-vs-contract mismatch (Interlink/Maestro) — since catalog growth alone will not fix them.
